newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Dow boosts Eurobourses, Frankfurt hits peak.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dow boosts Eurobourses, Frankfurt hits peak.

text.p: Wall Street's bull run, marked by a sixth consecutive record close overnight, boosted European bourses on Thursday and helped leading German shares to open at a new peak.

On the currency markets the dollar was steady against the mark but firmed against the yen after Japan's "Mr Yen", senior finance ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara, welcomed a rising dollar and said Tokyo's foreign exchange policy had not changed.

New York's performance gave an early impetus to European equities. The Dow Jones industrial average closed up 8.20 points at 6,274.24 after the Federal Reserve decided to keep U.S. interest rates unchanged. The Dow has surged 245 points, or four percent, since the start of the month

In Frankfurt German shares extended their rising trend and pre-bourse electronic dealings began at a new record high with the 30-share IBIS DAX index opening at 2,783.76 points and then moving further ahead. The trend continued in floor trading where the DAX-30 also passed a new trading peak.
Major share movers were Commerzbank, up over five percent on continuing merger speculation, and Deutsche Bank and Dresdner Bank also up on higher volumes.
After a disappointing performance on Wednesday, prompted by rising interest rate fears, London shares opened higher, pepped up by Wall Street and positive company news.

However, they reversed their early 12-point gain and the blue chip FTSE 100 index fell into negative territory after the release of figures showing stronger-than-expected British inflation. Year-on-year inflation in October rose sharply to 2.7 percent from 2.1 percent in September.
The market was given some backbone by well-received second quarter results from British Telecom, and first half figures from South West Water and PowerGen.
News of Great Universal Stores 1.05 billion pound ($1.7 billion) takeover of Experian, a Californian supplier of credit, marketing and real estate information services, was also welcomed.

The Paris bourse also opened higher, lifted by Wall Street, and the spotlight was on insurer Axa and its rival UAP as the two requoted for the first time since announcing their merger on Monday. As expected, UAP soared at the open, rising 17 percent. Axa shares opened 2.21 percent lower.
On the foreign exchange front the dollar was seen well supported after U.S. Treasury Undersecretary Jeffrey Shafer said on Wednesday the U.S exchange rate policy had not changed.
"Our policy is to have a strong dollar," he said.

Jeremy Hawkins, chief economist at Bank America, commented: "Shafer's comments were some of the first indications we have seen of what U.S. policy is under the new Clinton administration. To that extent it provided an important boost for the dollar."

One focus of interest was the seemingly inexorable rise of the pound sterling, which was given a boost by the higher-than- expected UK inflation figures -- seen as a possible precursor to further British rate rises.

The pound had risen sharply on Wednesday after an unexpectedly large decline in UK jobless fuelled expectations of further rate rises. On Thursday it was trading at a fresh four-year high against the dollar of $1.6650. Traders said they saw $1.67 as the next psychological target.
CURRENCIES AT 1000 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5050 marks and 111.66 yen compared with 1.5041 marks and 111.38 yen late in Europe on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1000 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was down 6.0 at 3,920.9.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 7.05 at 2,224.24.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was up 10.13 at 2,783.56.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was at $383.30 in early European trade compared with $384.05 an ounce at the London close on Wednesday. Silver was also lower at $4.91. ($1=.6054 Pound)
